title: docs: check missing prompts in man-page examples
body:
Related: #26428.

Some man-page examples begin with bare Podman commands despite the documented convention of using `$` for 
normal-user commands and `#` for commands requiring root.

This change extends the existing man-page checker to report missing prompts with the offending source file and line number.

### Changes

- Check fenced blocks in EXAMPLE and EXAMPLES sections, including unlabelled blocks and blocks labelled sh, bash, shell, or console.
- Skip blank lines and `###` comments, then report bare `podman` or `sudo podman` commands on the first meaningful line.
- Track backtick and tilde fences so their contents are not interpreted as document headings.
- Correct prompts in 41 man-page source files and document the scope of the check in MANPAGE_SYNTAX.md.
- Add 28 regression cases and run them through `.check-self-tests`.

The existing cross-reference test also needs a repair to its fault-injection setup. Its volume-prune fault injection searches for `driver` and `opt` rows that were removed from volume-prune man page. Use the existing `label` and `until` rows instead, preserving the checks for a misplaced negated filter and a duplicate filter entry.

### Scope

The check examines only the first meaningful line of each supported example block. It does not validate every command, determine whether root privileges are required, execute examples, or require output.

Regression cases cover valid prompts, missing prompts, output containing Podman commands, continuations, here-documents, scripts, PowerShell prompts, and fence handling.
